items.item_text: California Board of Pharmacy Technician License
Certified Pharmacy Technician (CPhT) from the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board (PTCB)
Minimum education satisfied through attainment of the required licensure/certification
Recent inpatient pharmacy experience, including pharmacy receiving or inventory
Experience teaching and evaluating the performance of pharmacy technicians and students
Experience training or mentoring staff, serving as a technical resource, coordinating workflow, resolving operational issues, or supporting daily operations
Experience working with Pyxis and EPIC Systems for data retrieval, billing and problem solving
Experience managing and leading of multiple staff members
Experience with DSCSA, BD Pharmacy Logistics (PLX), and inventory receiving

Responsible for on-line supervision of inpatient technician 2s and 3s. Responsible for daily management of operations. Responsible for supervision, staff development and assessment of staff competency for technicians. Responsible for technician student training in these areas. Manages daily scheduling of technicians and duty assignments. Works with the Inpatient Assistant Chief - Acute Care Operations, Central Pharmacy Managers and Inpatient Pharmacy Supervisors to identify areas of improvement and solutions through integration of pharmacy resources. Responsible for investigation and remedy of incident reports in responsible areas. Staff consists of professional, technical and administrative support personnel. The Technician staff fills first doses and batch doses for both IV and UD meds, refills Pyxis machines, deliver medications to nursing areas, problem solves medication distribution issues with nursing staff, and performs maintenance and inventory functions. This position may require staffing during times of staffing shortages. #CA-DS
70% - Supervisory, Administrative Tasks and Customer Service
Basic knowledge of automatic dispensing machine systems (PYXIS)

Decision-making skills to independently exercise delegated authority to take action, and to recognize when it is appropriate to seek assistance from others when limits of delegated authority have been reached

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem, identify the resources available to help solve the problem, create and implement viable solutions, and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved to the satisfaction of all parties

Interpersonal skills to establish and maintain a friendly, welcoming environment for departments and customers to demonstrate an interested, understanding, compassionate manner, to maintain a courteous and calm demeanor, and to use a proactive approach to negotiate with and persuade others to take required action
